title: The Hole in the Sky
synopsis: A small square of the sky goes missing over the Tree Fort, and Finn is the only one who thinks it's a big deal.
plot:
Finn wakes up and notices a perfectly square patch of sky above the Tree Fort is gone. Not dark, not cloudy: absent. Through it he can see something like a ceiling. Jake says it's probably fine. Bubblegum measures it and says it's probably fine. Marceline flies up to it, touches it, and says it feels like a ceiling, and that it's probably fine.

Finn cannot let it go. He climbs to the top of the Tree Fort every night to stare at it. He starts dreaming about it. In the dream, the Cosmic Owl tells him that it isn't a hole, it's a window, and that someone on the other side is looking in. Finn wakes up and decides to wave at it.

Nothing happens for a week. Then, one night, the square blinks. Finn wakes Jake. They watch it together. It blinks again, slowly, like an eye that has just noticed it is being noticed. Then it fills back in with ordinary sky, stars and all. Prismo, asked later, says he has no idea what it was and that Finn should probably stop waving at things he doesn't understand. Finn keeps waving anyway, just in case.
transcriptText:
Finn: Jake. Jake. Look up.
Jake: [looking] It's sky.
Finn: That part. The square part.
Jake: Huh. That's a square of no sky. Probably fine.
Finn: HOW is that probably fine?!
Princess Bubblegum: [with instruments] It's exactly four meters on a side. Perfectly square. Zero light emission. Fascinating. Probably fine.
Finn: Why does everyone keep saying that!
Marceline: [floating up to it, tapping it] Feels like a ceiling. Kinda drywall-y.
Finn: DRYWALL?
Marceline: Probably fine.
[Night. Finn sits alone on the roof, staring up.]
Finn: What are you?
[Dream. The Cosmic Owl hovers.]
Cosmic Owl: It's not a hole, Finn.
Finn: Then what is it?
Cosmic Owl: It's a window. Someone's looking in.
Finn: Looking at what?
Cosmic Owl: [shrugs] You, I guess.
[Finn wakes up.]
Finn: [to the sky] Hi.
[He waves. Nothing happens.]
[A week later. Finn is still waving.]
Jake: Dude, you've been waving every night for a week.
Finn: Just in case.
[The square blinks.]
Finn: JAKE. JAKE, IT BLINKED.
Jake: [scrambling up] It did what now?
[They watch. It blinks again. Slowly. Then fills in with stars.]
Jake: ...Okay. Okay, that was not probably fine.
Finn: [still waving] Bye!
[The Time Room.]
Prismo: No idea, man. Genuinely no idea. Maybe stop waving at stuff you don't understand?
Finn: What if it was lonely?
Prismo: ...Okay, keep waving.
